frontmatter.name: openspec-apply-change
frontmatter.description: Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change. Use when the user wants to start implementing, continue implementation, or work through tasks. Also use when the user says "openspec apply", "opsx apply", or "openspec implement".

frontmatter.name: openspec-archive-change
frontmatter.description: Archive a completed OpenSpec change in the experimental workflow. Use when the user wants to finalize and archive a change after implementation is complete. Also use when the user says "openspec archive" or "opsx archive".

frontmatter.name: openspec-propose
frontmatter.description: Propose a new OpenSpec change with all artifacts generated in one step. Use when the user wants to quickly describe what they want to build and get a complete proposal with design, specs, and tasks ready for implementation. Also use when the user says "openspec propose" or "opsx propose".

frontmatter.name: openspec-sync-specs
frontmatter.description: Sync delta specs from an OpenSpec change to main specs. Use when the user wants to update main specs with changes from a delta spec, without archiving the change. Also use when the user says "openspec sync" or "opsx sync".

frontmatter.name: openspec-update-change
frontmatter.description: Update an OpenSpec change by revising its existing planning artifacts and keeping them coherent with one another. Use when the user wants to revise a change's plan, fold new decisions into it, or reconcile its artifacts after an edit. Also use when the user says "openspec update change" or "opsx update". If the user means the openspec update CLI command, which refreshes generated files, run that command instead. Never edits code.

frontmatter.name: openspec-verify-change
frontmatter.description: Verify implementation matches OpenSpec change artifacts. Use when the user wants to validate that implementation is complete, correct, and coherent before archiving. Also use when the user says "openspec verify" or "opsx verify".

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Prefer graphify query/path/explain over raw grep or GRAPH_REPORT.md because they return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than the full report or raw source browsing; run graphify update after code changes since it is AST-only and incurs no API cost.

nodes.label: Container Security Hardening
nodes.rationale: Apply defense-in-depth and least-privilege to the production container: read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities (cap_drop ALL), no-new-privileges, tmpfs for writable paths, and running as non-root UID 1000 to limit blast radius if the app or web server is compromised.
